evidence.claim: Its unusual number connects the road to the observatory at Sunspot: 6563 is the hydrogen-alpha wavelength in angstroms used to study the Sun’s chromosphere and locate solar flares.
evidence.quote: It takes its number from the wavelength of the Hydrogen-alpha spectral line (6563 Å) used by scientists at the observatory to study the solar chromosphere and to locate solar flares on the Sun.

evidence.claim: In 2011, the observatory added planet signs spaced as a scale model of distances in the solar system.
evidence.quote: The solar observatory added signs along the highway in 2011 with the names of the planets as part of a 1:250 million model of the distances between planets in the Solar System.

evidence.claim: Sunlight traveled down a vacuum tube to a primary mirror 193 feet below ground, then returned to an optical laboratory at ground level.
evidence.quote: An entrance window at the top of the tower, and two mirrors, reflect sunlight down the vacuum tube to the 64-inch primary mirror, 193 feet (59 m) underground. The primary mirror focuses the light and reflects it back up, where it exits the vacuum tube through six quartz optical windows in the floor of an optical laboratory at ground level.

evidence.claim: A mercury bearing supported the rotating instrument.

flags: The dated February 2026 closure and planned dismantling in the Dunn telescope cache conflict with older open-site and tour claims in tourism and Sunspot pages. No reopening or completed demolition is documented. Confirm access with the site manager before publication; checked records cache review only.
Apache Point is a separate observatory with restricted buildings and telescopes; no public tour or solar-observatory identity is inferred for it.
Road construction history is absent. Overview history uses the supported road number, byway designation and 2011 planet signs.
The tourism page uses 15 miles, the highway page 15.530 miles and material a 16.1-mile mapped corridor; used tourism’s drive length without inventing an approximation.

Dropped the unsupported hedge about 15 miles. Omitted the sourced but anonymous Dirty Drawers naming story and allegedly rigged Sunspot vote because they lack named attribution and do not develop the central story.
Planet signs extend along the route rather than occupying one documented point. Kept the existing Haynes/planets/Sunspot sequence without inventing coordinates or a single turnout.
